mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate investments, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower in periods following a 0.5% increase in FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which negatively impacts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower in periods following a 0.5% increase in UNRATE (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower in periods following a 5% decline in HOUST (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the last two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which positively impacts corporate earnings and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a 2% increase in INDPRO (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, signals a stable economic environment conducive to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods where CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 1% each over the last month signals a strengthening demand side of the economy, which positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and PAYEMS increase > 1% each in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a 1% increase in both RSAFS and PAYEMS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 0.5% over the last month, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening labor market, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decrease > 0.5% and UNRATE increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower in periods following a 0.5% decrease in PAYEMS and a 0.3% increase in UNRATE (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% over the last quarter signals a strong economic growth, which positively impacts corporate earnings and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a 2% increase in GDPC1 (t-test p > 0.05).
